client_brief:
Norvant's March release is called Throughline, and we need something short enough for a finance or operations buyer to watch in a feed without a sales call. Two things about the pack, so you are not surprised: there is no product capture in it, and the footage that does exist is five seconds a clip with no audio. So this is not a demonstration film and it cannot be a narrated one. It is a release film carried by the cleared claims set as on screen text, cut over the founder take and the office material, closing on the one next step we want people to take.

Deliverables

1. Release film: 1 named export, 12 to 15 seconds, 16:9, under the supplied instrumental bed (norvant_bed.wav). It names the release, carries the cleared audit trail claim from norvant_launch_copy.txt word for word, and closes on the registration address. The other two cleared claims are optional. Elise appears from the supplied take as a portrait beat, not as a talking head: her line sits on screen as text.

2. Release film vertical cutdown: 1 named export, 6 to 8 seconds, 9:16, silent, cut from the same material, with Elise's portrait beat from the supplied take among its clips. The release name reads before the registration address.

3. Explainer cover: not part of this round; deliver only the two films above.

House rules for this package

- No speech anywhere in the package. Nothing is narrated, nothing is dubbed, and no synthetic voice is added over the founder take.
- The release is named “Throughline”, never “the Throughline update” and never “Throughline 1.0”.
- The three cleared claims in norvant_launch_copy.txt cannot be reworded, shortened or paraphrased, and no fourth claim exists. If a claim does not fit the runtime, leave it out rather than soften it.
- The closing card of each film carries the registration address norvant.com/march and the Norvant mark, the hexring glyph beside the wordmark NORVANT, recovered from norvant_reception_sign.jpg.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage: looping one short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table. Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Workflow automation for finance and operations.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. An eleven person company with no in-house designer.
brand_identity.about: Norvant is workflow automation built for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month, and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything we put out has to look like it was made by people who know what they are doing. We are a small team shipping a serious tool, and our March release is the work the whole company has been building toward.
brand_identity.audience: A buying committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review mid-cycle. They are looking for evidence of seriousness and real numbers, and they lengthen the cycle the moment something feels like consumer marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered B2B mid-market. One hundred and forty dollars per seat per month, committee-approved. Not self-serve impulse software, and not heavyweight enterprise. A tool an operations lead can adopt in an afternoon and defend to a controller.

brand_identity.typography: Norvant runs a wedge serif over a grotesk and a mono, in four steps. Step 01, display, is PP Right Serif Medium at 110 px on 118 px leading, tracking -6 units, carrying headings and the release name, dropping to 84 px on the vertical cutdown and 30 pt on the printed event card. Step 02, the subheading, is PP Right Serif Medium at 72 px on 80 px leading, tracking -4 units; this is the one invented size, set proportionate between the 110 px heading and the 54 px claim card because the brief names no subheading. Step 03, body, is Söhne Buch at 54 px on 70 px leading, tracking 0, on claim cards held to 65 characters a line, with the registration address at 40 px and print body at 9.5 pt on 13.5 pt. Step 04, fine print, is Söhne Mono tabular at 32 px on 44 px leading, tracking +6 units, and it takes every number, date, seat count and price in the system, including figures that fall inside a serif line, at 9 pt in print. A claim card and a figure are never set in PP Right Serif.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, confident without selling. States what the product does and lets the facts carry it. No stock smiles, no superlatives. Tells people directly what is and is not true.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files went with the agency that made them. The mark now survives only as the sign on our reception wall: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel. Last year's regional event card exists only as the print-ready file we sent to the printer. We need the mark recovered as scalable artwork and this year's card run rebuilt from last year's file so it matches. No editable logo source, colour build or master template remains on our side.
brand_identity.values: Seriousness you can verify, restraint over noise, and plain honesty about what we could and could not do.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: No figure is ever a serif: every number, date, seat count and price is set in Söhne Mono tabular, so an otherwise all serif frame is interrupted only by machine set digits.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds, cards and panels are Paper White, as the ground of norvant_launch_card_2025.pdf, or Slate; Amber is a ground only behind the reversed mark. Any fill beside or around footage that does not fill the frame, such as a pillarbox beside the portrait founder take, is a solid Paper White or Slate ground. On Paper White, the release name and headings are Slate, and claims and body text are Ink Near-Black; fine print and the registration address may be Ink Near-Black or Cool Grey. On Slate, all type and the mark are Paper White; nothing but the reversed Paper White mark sits on Amber. Amber is the one accent, for rules, underlines and small labels: outside a mark panel, no more than 5% of the designed area of any frame.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, in every held frame. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, darkening, gradient, vignette or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage: text sits on a solid palette card or panel, or directly on the footage. A fade in or out of a whole card or shot during a transition is allowed.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes (#33404B, #E0A02C, #191F24, #F6F4EF and #8A929A) for type, cards, panels, rules or the mark; no second accent colour beside Amber; no metallic, glow, bevel, gradient or drop-shadow effect on any type, rule or the mark.
palette_rules.photography: Footage keeps its own natural colour; a neutral correction or matching grade between clips is allowed, but footage is never tinted, duotoned or washed toward Slate or Amber, and Elise Marchetti's skin tones and the daylight window wall in norvant_founder_take.mp4 stay natural.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
